text.p: Leading Lithuanian brewer Utenos Beverages said on Monday that its net profit in 1996 fell a bit to 7.2 million litas from 7.5 million litas the previous year.

The company also said that it expected its profit to dip again in 1997 as it plans to launch an agressive sales and marketing campaign to maintain its leading position in the share of the thirsty Lithuanian beer market.

"We plan that our net profit in 1997 will be 6.5 million litas since we shall put more money in the development of sales and adveritising of our product this year," the chairman of Utenos Beverages Arunas Lubys told Reuters by phone.
He added that the company decided to pay 12 percent per share in dividends for 1996.
Lubys also said that the company planned to invest around 5.2 million litas in upgrading its production lines and marketing this year.
"We had 35 percent of the country's beer market in 1996 and produced 400,000 hectolitres of beer last year," Lubys said.
